I have been farming these same 5 mu for 40 years. My eyes are not so sharp now, and my back hurts, but I know this land. My son works in town and sends some money, so I manage with my daughter-in-law's help in busy times.

Last year I got about 450 jin of wheat per mu and a bit more maize. I will do the same as last year — why change when it worked?

For my wheat, I sow in October after the maize comes off. I buy seed from the same dealer my neighbor uses — the bag says it is a good new kind, I cannot read it but the dealer shows me. Before sowing I spread 2 bags of the compound fertilizer, the one with three 15s on the bag. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I spread 2 bags of urea — one bag now is about 80 yuan, so that is 160 yuan just for urea, but without it the wheat is yellow and weak. I water 4 times: once before winter so the roots set, then at green-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I spray maybe 2 times — once for the aphids that come in spring, once if I see the red spots on leaves.

For maize, I plant right after the wheat combine leaves in June. No ploughing — who has time, and it costs to hire the tractor. I just drop the seed behind the machine. The seed bag says hybrid, the dealer picks a kind the neighbors are planting. I put 2 bags of compound at sowing and 1.5 bags of urea when the maize is knee-high. I water twice if the rain does not come — the well is there, I just pay for the electricity. I spray once for the borer worms, sometimes twice if I see the holes in the leaves.

I always use a little more fertilizer than some neighbors say is needed. If I put too little and the harvest is bad, I have nothing. If I put a bit too much, I only lose some money on the bag. That is why I do not cut down.
